The club's finances consist of revenues from tickets, transfers, advertising and expenditure on salaries and taxes.

215449.overview: Bosse Des Maths 4ème is an educational adventure game in French, developed and published by Coktel Vision, which was released in Europe in 1987.

215614.overview:
Long Lance: A Computer Game of Tactical Naval Combat in the South Pacific is a strategic naval simulation of Japanese and American forces in the South Pacific during World War II.

Designed for 1 - 2 players, each player controls either the American or Japanese forces. A computer opponent is available for 1-player games. The viewpoint is of the theater naval commander, and the player composes task forces, establishes missions and destinations for those groups, and responds to operational events.

The game is text-only, and came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units. Gameplay includes Savo Island on 9 August 1942, Cape Esperance on 11 October, Guadalcanal on 13 November, Guadalcanal on 14 November, and Tassafaronga on 30 November. Time passes in 20 minute intervals, allowing the player to input new commands for their fleet, but will stop to allow the player to react to enemy movements. Gameplay consists of nighttime battles, and each scenario begins at 1800 and ends at 0600 the next morning.

During each gameplay segment, the player sets taskforce management, where the player can combine and split ships from each group to create new groups. The player also sets movement orders for their ships. The player adjusts battle doctrine for each group, including open/close range rules, rules of engagement, and tactical guidance. The player's vessels then follow their commanding officer's directions for a 20 minute interval, at which point they await new orders.

217267.overview: LUMA is laser based sliding puzzle game for Commodore Amiga where the goal is to connect lasers to targets of same color by using mirrors to deflect the beam. Activate the lasers using batteries. Each level must be solved within a specific amount of moves (shifts).

217490.overview:
Rudolphine Rur (Rudolph to friends) is in an enviable situation. He owns his own tree house in the most elegant part of the Valley. He has managed to progress in his profession to become respected as a Master Shoemaker. His family is in good health and he generally gets along with all of them (ahem). It looks like it's going to be a happy autumn in the Valley...
What will drive Rudolphine to leave his comfortable home and dash through intricate forests and snowy mountains until dangerously deep into the unpleasant human world?   
 
This game belongs to what came to be called conversational adventures, and which today is also known as interactive fiction. You will be able to move through a series of locations, each of them made up of a description and a small static graphic on some occasions. The game consists of exploring this world that the game offers you, interacting with the characters you meet, collecting and using the objects... in short, doing everything that allows you to overcome the challenges of the story and have a fun time with it.

The way to give orders is simple: you must write what you want to do, in a simple way, so that the computer understands you. Basically using the formula VERB + NOUN E, as for example:

get book

examine knife

hit plant

Occasionally you will need to use more complicated structures:

 open door with yellow key

give cheese to fox

The game has a large but limited vocabulary, so if you're sure of something but the computer doesn't understand you, try writing it differently or using different words. It will surely work.

They are basic commands in an adventure:

LOOK (M) , describes the current location again.

NORTH (N), SOUTH (S), EAST (E), WEST (O), NORTHWEST (NO), UP, DOWN... to move from one place to another.

219817.overview:
The Daring Rescue of Pacuvia the Sheep is a short, bizarre, traditional interactive fiction game for C64, Amiga, MS-Dos, Windows and Tandy Model 100. But it's also something more, it's a - drumroll - sentimental research project!

Your character is an operative of a mysterious “Agency”, on a dangerous mission: rescuing the bioengineered sheep called Pacuvia from the clutches of a guy too idiot to understand what he's got. Strapped of all your digital support for security reasons, you'll have to rely on your good ol' analogic equipment to recover Pacuvia. And don't forget she's not necessarily helpless...

219822.overview: Libyans in Space is a defender-like horizontal shooter released on Amiga in 1987.

219902.overview: Lightforce: You've read enough back covers to know that nothing should be believed.... Do yourself a favor and insert the enclosed disk in the nearest Amiga, and enjoy the most innovative and fun package, involving Strategy. Huge destruction, Progressive learning, Lateral thinking, and impressive graphics. Putting this box back on the shelf will mean you are missing out on one helluva good time.

278980.overview: Four Nintendo Game & Watch handheld games: Octopus, Parachute, Fire Attack and Oil Panic. Press Alts and Shifts to play. Written in 6 months.

418070.overview:
The 4 software programs in this collection address the ESSENTIAL knowledge of geometry, measurements and functions for the levels considered:
Lines and segments/Parallels and perpendiculars / Median line of a segment / Quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, rhombus) / Triangles / The circle and the disc/ Secants and tangents / Angles (measurements and particularities) / Axes of symmetry / The paving stone and the cube / Problems on areas / Problems on volumes. 

Units of length / Units of masses and capacities / Problems on scales / Problems of perimeters / Units of areas / Units of volumes / Shifts on an axis / Markings in the plane (abscissa, ordinate, negative numbers) / Examples of graphic functions.
Properties of parallelograms / Corresponding, opposite, alternate angles.../ Vertices of the angles of a triangle / Circumscribed circle / Center of symmetry / Planes in space (parallel and perpendicular) / Development of solids / Pyramids, prisms, cylinders / Area of ​​the parallelogram, of the trapezium, of the disc.../ Problems on volumes. 

Usual units of the metric system / Scales / Perimeters / Units of time / Conversions of durations / Calculations on durations / Problems of speeds / Units of areas and volumes / Works in an orthonormal frame / Situations of proportionality: graphic representations.
Midpoint theorem / Orthogonal projections / Distance from a point to a straight line / Cosine / Triangular inequality / Particularities of triangles / Medians, medians, heights, bisectors / Pythagorean theorem and its converse / Complex polygons / Geometry in space / Sphere and ball / Vectors and translations/Rotations.

Usual units (lengths, masses, capacities, areas, volumes) / Calculations of perimeters, areas, volumes / Calculations on durations / Works in an orthonormal frame / Linear applications and proportionality/ Graphical representations of linear maps. Vectors and translations / Chasles' relation / Operations on vectors (addition, subtraction, multiplication) / Midpoint of a vector / Trigonometry in the right triangle cosine, sine, tangent / Complementary angles / Thales' theorem and its converse / Transformations (translations, symmetries, rotations) / Inscribed angle, central angle / Measurement of an arc of a circle / Pyramids and cones. Revisions on the usual units (lengths, masses, capacities, durations, areas, volumes) / Calculations of areas and volumes / Distance of two points in an orthonormal frame / Line equations / Direction coefficient / Affine applications (properties, determination) / Graphical resolution of equations. 

Each software includes around thirty different modules, hundreds of exercises and associated aids. You also have a calculator, a notepad and an electronic calendar. "CONTROLS" modules allow you each quarter to check and note the progress of the achievements. The "REVIEWS" show you the progress made as well as the weak points to work on.

418352.overview: The game is a weird mix of all kinds of genres. The first part is a horizontal shooter/platformer, while the second part is a point-and-click adventure which you need to find a solution to. Knowledge of Spanish language is not needed in the first part, but in the point-and-click adventure part, it is even mandatory, as the great part of hints will be given by speech only.

418376.overview:
A single player PD\Freeware adventure game from Asa Margetts and David Charman. The game begins in 1947; there was a kingdom far, far away,
situated in a location only known to few. In the kingdom lay the king himself, he was old and dying, you are his son, at the tender age of 10, you look after his grey with brown patched dog. This dog meant more to the king then anyone could know. Jaharra, the meanest ,roughest guy in the land was at war with the King, but always got the worst when battling him. He needed to get at the king. 1950: after 3 years of planning, he fought and managed to kidnap the king's dog. He took him away and slaughtered the poor dog. You and the king were devastated. The King took ill from it and died. But you promised you would find the evil Jaharra and escort him to his grave.

418387.overview: A single player, freeware crosshairs shooter that can be controlled with a Trojan Phazer light gun. It is the precursor to L.E.D. Clones II (Assault on Obsidian Base) and came out in 1991.

418399.overview: A homebrew Tron\Worm\Snake game created by Neil McKnight and released in 1992. There are no options in this game so you can't increase the difficulty, 25 levels in the game and there is no ending.

418422.overview: The City of Eilyk has risen into a state of panic. The Lost Chessboard of Eugonim has been stolen from its sacred hiding place. And the world as we know it is under threat. The Euil Innad has claimed responsibility for the dastardly deed and has demanded that the tood people of Eilyk surrender to their demands. He give everyone the same challenge. If you can pass the 50 mazes of his lair The Chessboard will be returned.

418426.overview: An arcade style Collect'em Up by Nigel Fredericks and released to the public domain in 1991.

418431.overview: Clone of a ZX Spectrum Jumping Jack game with 16-bit graphics and sound. Becomes very difficult later on due to the number of baddies onscreen. The game even asks "Aren't you getting fed up with this?" before the level with 18 baddies chasing you begins. When the number gets up to 20, it says "You must be cheating!"

418437.overview: This is a Boulder Dash related PD game, though gameplay is much different with this being more of an action game without the heavy BD puzzle element. It was created by Carsten Magerkurth who was part of German Operating System and released as freeware in 1992.

418531.overview:
Land of the Unicorn is an educational game for vocabulary practice that contains three activities: synonym review and quizzes, antonym review and quizzes and The Quest of the Silver Unicorn. The first two are for drilling and practising words while the third is the actual game.

In the quest game, the player controls a unicorn, Kelsany, who is looking for a magic necklace that will save his land from doom. The necklace can be found in one of five castles and the gameplay involves navigating through the maze-like gameworld and collect the keys that will open up each castle. As the player moves around the game will stop periodically and ask questions. There are multiple choice questions involving synonyms and antonyms and fill-in questions that involve anagrams. By answering questions correctly the player is awarded with gold. The gold is needed to pay bridge trolls who otherwise prevent the player from crossing rivers. The game ends when the player unlocks the door leading to the castle that contains the necklace.

418578.overview: Let's Spell at the Shops is one of three games in the Let's Spell series of educational games that teaches letter recognition and spelling. They all feature the same gameplay but has different settings. The player explores the setting (which consists of multiple scenes) and clicks on various objects. After clicking on an object, the player is prompted to spell it correctly by clicking on the right letters in the alphabet. There are two levels of play: one for a lower age group (4-6) where the word is spelled out from the start and one for slightly older children (ages 6-9) who has to figure out the spelling themselves. The harder level still has a hint options though that briefly shows the correct spelling. This version's setting is a mall which consists of several different stores: groceries, toys, clothes, music etc.

418581.overview: Let's Spell Out and Above is one of three games in the Let's Spell series of educational games that teaches letter recognition and spelling. They all feature the same gameplay but has different settings. The player explores the setting (which consists of multiple scenes) and clicks on various objects. After clicking on an object, the player is prompted to spell it correctly by clicking on the right letters in the alphabet. There are two levels of play: one for a lower age group (4-6) where the word is spelled out from the start and one for slightly older children (ages 6-9) who has to figure out the spelling themselves. The harder level still has a hint options though that briefly shows the correct spelling. This version consists of a variety of locations: town, farm, seaside, water world, country, zoo, winter wonderland and park.

418582.overview: Choose from four skill levels in the unique jigsaw puzzle challenge. Not only does the picture animate when finished, but it is animated prior to putting the pieces in, meaning an additional level of difficulty, but sometimes helping hand for where a piece should be located on the puzzle mat.

418731.overview: Zelda as an unfinished "Prototype" for the Commodore Amiga by Tukinem.

418756.overview: Lykkehjulet is the Danish version of the Wheel of Fortune television game show. It has over 2000 ORD!

419542.overview:
Land of Genesis is a platformer shoot'em up created by Maurizio Gemelli with Andreas Stürmer providing the music and SFX. It was published in 2001 by ClearWater Interactive for Amiga AGA and Amiga CD machines. Maurizio Gemelli was a former demoscene developer for the Amiga, and he spent three years programming this fantastic action game clearly inspired to Turrican. Land Of Genesis was distributed on CD only and required a very powerful Amiga (at least 68020 with 4MB, but better to have a 68040 with 8MB Fast RAM to enjoy the extended version). The game featured 5 massive levels and all sorts of special effects including 3D video, 512 colors on the screen, 180 different enemies controlled by their AI, plenty of parallax scrolling, and transparent backgrounds.

The game was criticized for the extreme difficulty, so you might want to at least change the settings to Easy in the options screen.

419630.overview:
There are really all 33 (32 standard + 1 practice) levels for you to play. Calimero: just some clever coding + own gfx cruncher/generator (which took quite some ... got 1st in the Breakpoint 2005 96K Game competition. Like the original, this is an Amiga car racing game. There are 19 computer opponents (15 on the 8-bit versions) and you have to finish in the top 10 (top 8 on the 8-bits) to progress. The higher you finish in one race, the lower down the grid you start for the next race. The opposition drivers have pun names based on the F1 drivers of the day - examples include Ricardo Pastry and Crashhard Banger.

You can choose between sound effects or one of a variety of music pieces. The game features a simultaneous 2-player mode, but the 1-player mode only uses half the screen, a simple animation filling the other half. In most races you will have to make a pitstop for fuel in order to reach the finish. The tracks include features such as oil slicks, roadworks, boulders and rivers - contact with these (or the other cars) will slow you, but there is no car damage model.

420577.overview: After the events that occured in Termina and the victory of the hero on his evil alter-ego, Zelda and Link knew that, from the bottom of hell, Ganon the immortal drawed his power from his wish to the Triforce, and rounded up his army with a view to invade Hyrule. Until the day when, after months spent watching out for an attack, an event came up and put an end to this endless waiting...

420619.overview:
A fan name Zelda clone which is a sequel to Legend of Zelda: Time to Triumph, this is the fourth in the line of fan-made Zelda games is again on the harder side, and introduces a trading element, and also a friendly fairy; who can restore your health.  
 
At the end of Time To Triumph, Link left Hyrule to take well-deserved holidays far from the kingdom’s restlessness. Link set sail to discover distant lands and paradise islands where he gladly spent the many rupees he had borrowed from the princess. Yet, he’s holidays took a decisive turn on a small island where he heard interesting rumors. Those rumors were about a very special island, the most fabulous beach resort ever discovered, the marvelous Fairy Island. Link was very curious about it, and set sail again to see it by himself. But what he found there wasn’t quite what he expected: a quick and painful death killed by a sea monster. His body washed ashore on a beach. Is it the end of Link’s adventures? Maybe, unless the young fairy incoming on this beach can change Link’s destiny and prepare him for a new adventure.

420628.overview: After Link’s victory over Ganon (in “A Link to thePast”),no one knows what Link’s wish to the Triforce was. But this wish reunified the Light World and the Dark World and brought the 7 wise men’s descendants back to life. Peace was back in Hyrule. But unfortunately, this wish also ressurected Ganon and his henchmen. He was preparing his revenge, but he couldn’t do anything without the Triforce. One night, a familiar voice speaks to Link in his sleep…

420631.overview: This, the second game in the series is more difficult that Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian, and gives us the ability to transform into Oni Link when close to death, and this provides a fire sword and a fighting chance to come back. The enemies are easy, but temples are made harder by having to walk around in circles, and trigger buttons far away to make any progress. There is a hidden switch also, and having to fight two bats with just one skull. Precursor to Legend of Zelda: Time to Triumph.

420718.overview:
This is my submission to the AmiGameJam 2022 which had the theme Swords and Sorcery. You have previously nearly reached the end of your quest. All that stands in your way now is The Last Dungeon!

Choose your character, Barbarian or Wizard, or team up together in 2 player co-op. Explore the maze like like dungeon mapping each room as you go.
Fight or avoid the dungeon guardians waiting for you inside. Press fire to attack. Hold fire THEN a direction to use your second item. Rooms will reveal secrets to the curious! Good luck on your quest brave adventurer!!!

420823.overview: A graphic adventure by José A. González, released in 2017.

420959.overview: Guide the colored balls home in this 5 level game. Similar concept to that of lemmings in this 1192 shareware game by Charles Chapman.

420982.overview: A funky tool released at TRSAC 2002 intended to allow you to lay out a LEGO project or design in the virtual space.

421196.overview: The programmer of this game launched a legal action against Rockstar North for alleged copyright violation due to the similarity of Grand Theft Auto to Crime Inc. and the fact that he had given them a demo of the game for consideration. A top down gangster themed game that was never finished.

421261.overview:
Laser World is a puzzle board game, set in 2287. As a laser tank driver, Lieutenant Hickman, the player must destroy all compact disks before the time runs out. Achieving the task requires moving mirrors and other elements to the right place. The game features numerous elements, such as: * block (stationary element reflecting the laser beam at an angle of 90 degrees)

    mirror (sliding element reflecting the laser beam at an angle of 90 degrees)
    laser (ray generator)
    compact (an element that needs to be destroyed)
    laser switch on/off (laser hit switch off generator, tank must enter it to switch it on)
    extra life (adds one life)
    exit (needs to be hit with a laser to go to the next level)
    absorbing block (a stationery element, absorbing laser beam)
    sluice (moves tank two field)
    laser sluice (only laser beam may go through it)
    bomb (a sliding element destroying all object one field far)
    teleport (moves tank to another place)
    extra time (add more time to complete the level)

421362.overview: Scheduled for release in 1991, the game was cancelled when the project ran overtime and bugs in the code still remained unresolved. One becomes three. Anyone who buys Ubisoft's "Light Quest" gets three games at once. Basically, it's once again about freeing a fantasy kingdom from the clutches of demonic forces. However, whether you take on the fight against the evil Zora and her hordes of monsters as a warrior, as a cute Heinzelmann or as a magician is up to you. Depending on which form you choose, Lightquest presents itself as a thoroughbred action game, a thinking-heavy adventure game.

421975.overview: A Spanish language word guessing game for one to four players from CopySoft Software Ltd. in 1997.

421976.overview: A Dutch puzzle word game. You must solve word puzzles in Dutch to be able to fill in a Bingo card to win. There are a couple of games like this, this one is by the Huissence Computer Club and released as public domain in 1989.

421984.overview: Lingo is a digital version of the TV game show of the same name. Like in the game show it is the objective to guess five letter words. You are only given the first letter. You get several tries and with each try the letters are marked which are correctly placed and those who appear in the word but at a different location. Within words you get to blindly draw a ball from a pool. There are 17 numbered balls that correspond with a numbers on a bingo card. There's a ball with a question mark that let the players pick a number at will. When the players complete a row or column they receive bonus points. There's also three red balls that passes the turn to the other player and three green balls. A green ball allows you to pick another ball and also when you get three green balls before the game is over you win a jackpot. The game starts with two players, but after some rounds the player with most points goes to the finale. The game is in Dutch so only features Dutch words. It contains a library of 15,000 words.

422176.overview: A freeware traditional paper-and-pencil, tabletop game created by Ben Knapp of Tracysoft International in 1993. The words are saved in a text file so you can make your own word lists!

422177.overview: A game similar to that of Pacman, collect items to complete the level but watch the bad guys. It is based on the Arcade Ladybug game and features the same gameplay of dot-eating, revolving doors, a cage letting out monsters and a smart bomb to kill them. It supports one or two plaers and a high score table. It was created by Erwin Van Den Berg, as a public domain game and has some nice 80's synth music you may recognize as New Order by Blue Monday.

422183.overview: Expand your Dominion across the stars. Conquer your enemies to claim that which is rightfully yours. A shareware game for one or two players by Mike Bryant with version 1.3 coming out in 1993.

422184.overview: A one or two player freeware game created in C by Tim Pietzcker in 1991. It is a strategy puzzle game. It was included in the Assassins Game Disk #88 along with Smurf Hunt and "Legand of Lothian".

422187.overview: A freeware two-player, Boulder Dash style game created in greyscale by Kimmo Teräväinen in 1996.

422190.overview: A point and click adventure game, released as freeware by Sjef Rijnen in 1990.

422194.overview: A shareware soccer\football management game with cards for randomized events.

422197.overview: Legend of Lothian is an Ultima clone written by Cal Poly student David W. Meny and published via the September 1991 issue of the Amiga magazine, Jumpdisk.  King Lothian of Mercia once ruled a propsperous, peaceful kingdom, but one day he didn't wake up, and no method magical or mechanical could rouse him from his slumber. Without his leadership, the country fell to ruin and orcs roam the land freely. The game's main quest is, of course, to find a way to wake up Lothian. The character is a poor shepherd. One night, a bearded man visits his dreams and tells him that only he can awaken Lothian. The old man leaves a glowing gemstone behind which is still there when the character wakes up. He gathers what money he can and sets out the next day.

422213.overview: An AMOS based freeware game from Plastic Brain from 1991. Use the mouse to shoot weird looking people who pop up in windows. A game name based on that of an early computer virus.

422215.overview: A shareware text adventure game created by James Lean with AMOS and released in 1992. In Life After Death you control not one, but two characters, the young students of the supernatural, Orrin and Lena. Subsequently the problems within the game often require two people to solve them. You may freely swap between characters using the SWAP command, and it must be remembered that both have their own levels of strength and ability. You enter the afterlife in the 'Zone of Reality', in which various aspects of the real world are simulated. After the Zone of Reality you must cross the puzzle-bridge to the Zone of Fantasy, where human fantasies are real, and then on to the Gates of Hell and the end of the game. Along the way you will encounter various characters, and will have to solve many puzzles in order to progress.

422221.overview: A platform game made completely with letter symbols and ASCII code! There were several versions of this, 1.0 came out on May 28, 1991, with 1.1 coming out in 1996. The game came with a built in level editor. There were seven levels initially released. To stand still just jump to a location and hit any key other than the space or cursor keys.

422222.overview: Try to get Larry to the top by going up on the sliding platforms in this shareware game developed by C. Priestly and distributed by Perspective Public Domain in 1991.

422280.overview: A game created by The Judge and Melf of the the Bastards in 1991. A one or two player Snake game where you eat the blue dots without touching the walls, lines yourself or your opponent. Eating the blue dots increases your score and also the length of your snake.

422314.overview: A game in the style of Boulderdash or Emerald Mines crossed with Gauntlet created by Nick Jarrett and released as public domain in 1993.  Unlock and grab the diamonds, trade them for food or weapons.

422450.overview: A space shooter by Mikko Kallinen of Artificial People in 1998.

423058.overview: A Czech language text strategy based on a well-known TV series, Lost. It was created in 2010 by Mistic Joe of Crudesys.

423082.overview: A version of Scorched Earth on a hostile alien planet. Blast your enemy before they get you. A shareware game by Payton R. White from 1994. There are 25 levels in the registered version, only a handful without registration.

423087.overview: A bird's eye view, single player Roguelike. It is based off of an early mainframe game and was created and published by The Software Distillery in 1987 with 12 version updates being made. The game is one of the first Roguelikes (RPG dungeon crawls with top-down or isometric graphics and a high degree of randomization; Rogue or Nethack are examples) with a wilderness and more than one dungeon. In this game, you are searching the Caverns of Larn for a cure for your daughter's strange disease. The game world is presented entirely with ASCII text characters.

423124.overview: An action freeware game by Robsoft in 1991. A Worm\Snake style game, you can use the fire button to enter hyperspace, you only get one of those per game. The last one alive wins!

423175.overview: A one or two player Lunar Lander style game updated to graphics reminiscent of the Team17 Worms games. Your aim is to situate the lander over terrain sufficiently flat to land on and then, by firing thrusters left, right and down, guide it to rest with sufficiently gentle horizontal and vertical velocity that it doesn't dash itself to bits on the planet's surface. All that with limited fuel supplies!

423238.overview: An updated Czech language text strategy game where the goal is selling lemonade, becoming rich and buying a new iPhone, bike or laptop! With these humble beginnings a lemonade empire might be born, but only if you are wise and make the most of your resources.

423608.overview:
A 1988 shareware text adventure by Russel Wallace where you play the part of a character in the game. Many other characters are also in it. All characters, weapons and valuable objects computer-controlled characters, using the weapons. They will also be collecting weapons and using them against each other and you. You can can also collect valuable objects and drop them in a certain place to score points. If you outlive all the computer-controlled characters a new game will start and your score from the old one will be carried over into the new one. The rules of combat are exactly the same for you as anyone else your strength is depleted by blows and if it falls to zero you die. It will be replenished between fights but can never rise above your power. If you kill someone a quarter of their power is added to yours. 

Labyrinth II has many extra features over the original game. As with the original, most of the mobiles are named after people from my class in St. Andrews College, Blackrock, Co. Dublin. However, here part of the map is a taken from that place and other parts from various old adventure games. Some teachers from St. Andrews will appear in various locked rooms and can only be reached by finding the set of keys and unlocking the doors. You can only carry ten items at most. Defensive weapons (as opposed to offensive) powers will be combined when found, which will help keep your item count down and will work automatically to reduce the strength of blows against you. Treasures should be deposited aas soon as possible and will disappear from the game while incrementing your score. Try to find them before the other characters do.

423609.overview: An extensive Czech language text game by the Penline group, which took more than two years to develop. The game should run on every OCS Amiga, however with min. 1.5MB RAM. Unlike many other text adventures, here the player does not move around the game world only in the obligatory four directions north-south-west-east, but must choose, for example, to walk along a footpath, enter the forest, etc. which means, among other things, that even drawing the map is somewhat more difficult.

423630.overview: An educational game in French and English published by Carraz Editions in 1988. This program recognizes all English tenses characterized by their usual forms, whether active or passive, simple or continuous. Such forms as USED TO or WOULD expressing past habits, or various BE-phrases expressing future (BE GOING TO, BE ABOUT TO, BE TO), and modal auxiliaries other than those ordinarily used in future or conditional tenses, will not be recognized and should therefore be avoided.

423703.overview: A 1994 game written by Ivan Mladek, Roman Zezulak using GFA BASIC. Computer version of the Ivan Mládek's board game called Parliamentary lustration. Lustration law "is a special public employment law that regulates the process of examining whether a person holding certain higher public positions collaborated confidentially with the repressive apparatus of the communist regime."

423764.overview:
In the 13th century, the Catholic Church used it's soldiers to expel the members of the religious order of the Cathars from the Languedoc region of France. You, as Jean Raymond, have run from these soldiers and hidden in a Abbey. But it turns out the Abbey was built over catacombs of evil. Collect the twelve Cathar crosses to expel the evil from this building.

A game designed to look and control like a ZX Spectrum game. It's gameplay is inspired by games like Manic Miner and Jet Set Willy. You must move through room after room to find and gather the twelve crosses. Red hearts will grant you extra lives and stone pillars with a cross near the top act as checkpoints. Ring bells or move switches to open further passages. Avoid anything that is moving as it's touch will lose you a life. Lose all your lives and the game is over.

423825.overview: Earth is under attack! Everything has gone south, you are the Last Space Raider, a prototype is in your disposal to fight the enemy. You are earth last hope, may spirits be with you! A shooter in the style of an updated Space Invaders, but with aliens being added as you play some, way more difficult to eliminate.

423874.overview: A French language educational game for the Amiga developed and released by Carraz Editions in 1987.

423915.overview: A four-reel video slot\fruit machine brought to you as shareware by Gary Hunt in 1992.

424645.overview:
In the 13th century, the Catholic Church used it's soldiers to expel the members of the religious order of the Cathars from the Languedoc region of France. You, as Jean Raymond, have run from these soldiers and hidden in a Abbey. But it turns out the Abbey was built over catacombs of evil. Collect the twelve Cathar crosses to expel the evil from this building.

l'Abbaye des Morts (Abbey of the Dead) is a game designed to look and control like a ZX Spectrum game. It's gameplay is inspired by games like Manic Miner and Jet Set Willy. You must move through room after room to find and gather the twelve crosses. Red hearts will grant you extra lives and stone pillars with a cross near the top act as checkpoints. Ring bells or move switches to open further passages. Avoid anything that is moving as it's touch will lose you a life. Lose all your lives and the game is over.

448495.overview: Pix is a happy pixel part of a trending AMIGA video game. Until one day there is a blackout and comes out of the screen.

449840.overview: Light Bikes is a 1-player Tron Light Cycles game for the Commodore Amigs. It was developed by John Walke and published by CAM in 1987.

450107.overview: Lotto is a single-player Lottery simulation developed by Degra Software and released into the public domain in 1996.

451361.overview:
Luca Carminati of LC-Games, has released all of his Amiga games that he coded in the years 1995/1998.  

There's a space shooter, Croins, which looks a little bit like a classic Asteroids game, a Worms/Snake like Arcade game, Hyper Viper with lots of levels, collectable fruit and deadly skulls, Kangy, a family friendly platformer with a nice little soundtrack, Marietto a mario-esque popping arcade game, and finally Slalom Speciale, a Skiing simulator for those of you who enjoy a bit of winter sports.

452179.overview: Lazy Mines is a Minesweeper clone/variant developed by Lorens Younes and released into the public domain in 1994.

452376.overview:
A deluxe version of the Leisure Genius version of Monopoly, released commercially in Europe for up to six players. Enjoy this greatly enhanced computer adaption of everyone's favourite property game Play with friends, or with clever computer opponents or any combination of both (1-6 players). This game was also released on the BOARD GENIUS compilation pack for Amiga.  

All the rules and familiar elements of Monopoly Deluxe are incorporated. Select your activities from a menu bar on the screen with a press of a button, and the computer takes you through each step. The computer acts as your banker and auctioneer too and it even throws the dice for you! But can you beat it?

454419.overview: Last battle 2 a kung fu master type game. uses 2 buttons. 1 level demo. should work on OCS 1MB chip Amiga

456112.overview: Lost Treasure is a 1-2 player co-operative shooter developed by Ricky Derocher using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1995.

457478.overview:
This collection features the whole trilogy:

Lotus Esprit Turbo Challenge
Lotus Turbo Challenge 2
Lotus: The Ultimate Challenge

458828.overview: A text-adventure game for AGA Amiga computers

459020.overview: Released 28 June 2025 4th in the Posadas 2025 Homebrew Games competition

459776.overview: Transcode of Lock'n'Chase arcade version for 68000/020 amiga machines.

460590.overview: An interactive shooting game that takes place in the Old West.

461900.overview: A labarynth\maze game published in the September 1988 issue of AmigaMagazine OnDisk #02.

462209.overview: The game is based on Leisure Suit Larry 1 and Police Quest 1, both created and published by Sierra On-Line.

471081.overview: Lincity is a free and open-source construction and management simulation game, which puts the player in control of managing a city's socio-economy, similar in concept to SimCity

471869.overview: Loony Ledges is a new 8-bit style platform game for the Amiga 500.

480648.overview:
This is a text adventure for AmigaOS 1.3 or later, set in Victorian London. 
Solve the mystery of a disappearance by exploring, using objects from your 
surroundings, and interacting with the characters you encounter throughout
the game.

481193.overview: Amiga Lemmings (1991) Integrated Level Editor for 1P and 2P Levels.On the title screen, CUSTOM follows FUN, TRICKY, TAXING and MAYHEM, with a list of your own levels, for one or two players, and New Level to create one

481580.overview:
An in-game level editor for the Amiga game Lemmings 2: The Tribes, as a WHDLoad install for a hard disk. You make your own levels in the game's own view, with the game's terrain, objects and skills, test play them at once, and keep them as files you can share.
The editor integrates directly into the game engine, ensuring 100% authentic gameplay and physics.

481643.overview:
Features
   - Music and Sound Effects together. Finally!
   - Choose from all eight stage music tracks plus the main theme before each course.
   - Ten distinct two-tone opponent car paint schemes.

481713.overview:
LIFEFORCE (Konami 1986) - AGA Amiga port, V1.0
Ported to the Amiga by TjLaZer 2026

482821.overview:
Lady Bug for Amiga

A maze you can change — and enemies you can outwit.

Based on Universal’s 1981 arcade game, Lady Bug turns a maze chase into a game of quick decisions. Guide your ladybird around the paths, collect the dots and bonuses, and stay clear of the enemy insects and deadly skulls. Push the rotating gates to redirect a pursuit or open an escape route. Time your letter pickups to complete EXTRA for another life and SPECIAL for an extra credit in the original arcade rules.
